Class BaseView

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
javax.swing.JInternalFrame
edu.cnu.mdi.view.BaseView
All Implemented Interfaces:
IFeedbackProvider, IFileDropHandler, ComponentListener, FocusListener, MouseListener, ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, EventListener, Accessible, RootPaneContainer, WindowConstants
Direct Known Subclasses:
DrawingView, GeometrySliceDemoView, JsonView, LogView, MapView2D, NetworkLayoutDemoView, PlotView, SimulationView, VirtualView
public class BaseView extends JInternalFrame implements FocusListener, MouseListener, ComponentListener, IFeedbackProvider, IFileDropHandler
Base class for all MDI views.

A BaseView is a JInternalFrame hosted on the application's Desktop. Most views contain an IContainer that provides a "world" coordinate system and drawing/interaction support. Container-less views (e.g. log or config panels) are also supported.

Persistence key (VIEWPROPNAME)

Each view owns a stable string prefix used as the namespace for its persisted properties (position, size, visibility, etc.). The prefix is derived automatically from the view's title at construction time by sanitizeForKey(String). Subclasses that need a hand-chosen, title-independent key should override getPropertyName().

Why not use the title directly? Titles may contain spaces and special characters that are awkward inside XML property keys, and they can change between releases. The sanitised form is stable and safe.

Persistence format

Properties are written using dotted keys: prefix.x, prefix.y, prefix.w, prefix.h, prefix.visible, prefix.maximized. When reading back, the legacy non-dotted variants (e.g. prefixx, prefixvisible) are also accepted so that files saved by older versions of the framework continue to work.

File drag-and-drop

Drop support is activated by calling enableFileDrop(Predicate) in the subclass constructor (after super(...)). That single call installs a FileDropHandler on every appropriate surface — the container canvas, the scroll-pane viewport (when present), and the frame itself — and stores the filter. Subclasses then override filesDropped(List) to handle the accepted files. No other wiring is required. 

public MyView(Object... keyVals) {
    super(PropertyUtils.fromKeyValues(keyVals));
    enableFileDrop(f -> f.getName().endsWith(".csv"));
}

@Override
public void filesDropped(List<File> files) {
    openCsvFile(files.get(0));
}

Design notes

  • All property parsing happens once in BaseView.ViewInitConfig.from(Properties), keeping the constructor body straightforward.
  • Nested static helpers (BaseView.FrameConfigurer, BaseView.ViewContentBuilder, etc.) keep each responsibility isolated without requiring separate compilation units.

    • resolveContainer

      protected IContainer resolveContainer(Rectangle2D.Double worldSystem)
      Resolve the IContainer for this view.

      Resolution order:

      1. An IContainer instance stored directly in the properties under PropertyUtils.CONTAINER.
      2. A Class stored under PropertyUtils.CONTAINERCLASS, instantiated via its (Rectangle2D.Double) constructor.
      3. A default BaseContainer.
      Parameters:
      worldSystem - the initial world coordinate rectangle
      Returns:
      a non-null container

    • onFirstRealize

      public void onFirstRealize()
      Called exactly once, after the view has been fully constructed and registered with the ViewManager.

      For eagerly-created views this occurs during normal startup. For lazily-created views (see ViewConfiguration) it occurs the first time the user selects the view from the Views menu.

      The default implementation is a no-op. Subclasses may override to reconcile with shared application state or perform other one-time post-construction work.

    • enableFileDrop

      protected final void enableFileDrop()
      Activate file drag-and-drop for this view, accepting all dropped files.

      Equivalent to enableFileDrop(null). Every file the user drops on the view is forwarded to filesDropped(List) without any filtering.

      Call this from the subclass constructor after super(...).

      See Also:
      • enableFileDrop(Predicate)

    • enableFileDrop

      protected final void enableFileDrop(Predicate<File> filter)
      Activate file drag-and-drop for this view with a type filter.

      Installs a single FileDropHandler instance on every surface that can realistically receive a drop in this view:

      1. Container canvas — the primary drawing surface for container-backed views.
      2. Scroll-pane and its viewport — present when the view was constructed with a scroll pane; without this, drops on the scroll-bar gutters would be silently ignored.
      3. The view frame itself — a fallback that covers container-less views (e.g. log or config panels) and any area of the frame chrome not covered by the surfaces above.

      The supplied filter is stored via setFileFilter(Predicate) and is evaluated by FileDropHandler before filesDropped(List) is called. Files that do not match the filter are silently discarded; if every file in a drop is rejected, Swing renders the "no-drop" cursor so the user receives clear feedback.

      Usage pattern — call once from the subclass constructor, then override filesDropped(List):

      public MyView(Object... keyVals) {
    super(PropertyUtils.fromKeyValues(keyVals));
    enableFileDrop(f -> f.getName().endsWith(".csv"));
}

@Override
public void filesDropped(List<File> files) {
    openCsvFile(files.get(0));
}

      This method is final to guarantee that the surface coverage described above is always complete. Subclasses that need finer control (e.g. canvas-only drops) may call JComponent.setTransferHandler(TransferHandler) directly after calling this method.

      Parameters:
      filter - acceptance predicate applied to each dropped file; pass null to accept all files without screening

    • setFileFilter

      public void setFileFilter(Predicate<File> filter)
      Set the file filter used to screen dropped files.

      Prefer calling enableFileDrop(Predicate) rather than this method directly; enableFileDrop both stores the filter and installs the FileDropHandler on all required surfaces. This setter is part of the IFileDropHandler contract and is also useful when the filter needs to be swapped at runtime without reinstalling the handler.

      Specified by:
      setFileFilter in interface IFileDropHandler
      Parameters:
      filter - the acceptance predicate, or null to accept all files

    • filesDropped

      public void filesDropped(List<File> files)
      Called on the EDT when one or more accepted files are dropped on this view.

      The default implementation is a no-op. Subclasses that have called enableFileDrop(Predicate) should override this method to handle the dropped files. The list is never null and is never empty; the filter (if any) has already been applied.

      Specified by:
      filesDropped in interface IFileDropHandler
      Parameters:
      files - the accepted dropped files; never null, never empty

      public static void applyFocusFix(JMenu menu, BaseView view)
      Install a mouse-enter listener on menu that selects view when the mouse enters the menu.

    • getImageComponent

      public Component getImageComponent()
      The component that best represents this view as a static image, for screenshot/clipboard capture (see TakePicture).

      The default returns the container's drawable component, which is correct for ordinary item-based 2D views: for those, the container component already shows everything the view has to offer. Views whose visible content is not fully contained in that one component should override this. PlotView is the prototypical example: its title, legend, and axis labels live on the surrounding PlotPanel, not on the inner PlotCanvas the container exposes, so capturing the container component alone would silently drop them.

      This exists so callers that want "an image of this view" — a toolbar's camera button, a menu action, a future export feature — have one consistent, view-owned question to ask, instead of each caller re-deriving its own answer (or a shared utility like TakePicture having to special-case specific view/panel types itself).

      Returns:
      the component to capture as this view's image; the container's component if one is present, otherwise this view itself

    • addWestPanel

      public void addWestPanel(JComponent panel)
      Adds a component to the WEST slot of this view's content pane, expanding the frame width to accommodate it.

      Uses a double invokeLater to guarantee execution after all construction-time invokeLater calls have been processed — including BaseView's deferred setVisible and ViewConfiguration's placement call. A single invokeLater is not sufficient because the placement work is itself queued at the same EDT level as a naive single defer.

      Parameters:
      panel - the component to place in the WEST slot; must not be null
